pointers.sentence: The decorator `django.contrib.admin.action` stores its `location=`, one or a list, as the function's `"locations"`; `description_plural=` is the change list's text, `description=` the change form's, and both when no plural is given (`django/contrib/admin/decorators.py:action`).

`get_actions`, `ModelAdmin.get_action`, `ModelAdmin.get_action_choices` and `ModelAdmin.response_action` take `action_location=`, and each value of `get_actions` is an `Action`, a dataclass of the function, the name, both descriptions and the locations (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:Action`).

An override of `get_actions` or `get_action_choices` without `action_location=` is found by inspecting its signature at each call, warned of through `warn_about_implementation` with the file and line that define it, and called without the argument; such a `get_actions` gives a change form no actions (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin._get_actions_with_action_location`).

`ModelAdmin.show_facets` (5.0) gives each filter's choices the count of rows each would leave: under `ShowFacets.ALLOW`, the default, when the query string has `"_facets"`; always under `ShowFacets.ALWAYS`; never under `ShowFacets.NEVER` (`django/contrib/admin/views/main.py:ChangeList.__init__`; [Filters and search: `list_filter`, `search_fields` and `date_hierarchy`](../admin/filters.md)).

Since 5.0 `AllValuesFieldListFilter`, `ChoicesFieldListFilter`, `RelatedFieldListFilter` and `RelatedOnlyFieldListFilter` take several values of their parameter and mark each as selected (`django/contrib/admin/filters.py:RelatedFieldListFilter.choices`); the change list keeps every value of a key and joins them with OR (`django/contrib/admin/utils.py:build_q_object_from_lookup_parameters`).

`BaseModelAdmin.lookup_allowed` has taken the request as its third argument since 5.0, and `ChangeList.get_filters` passes it by position (`django/contrib/admin/views/main.py:ChangeList.get_filters`).
Since 5.1 a name of `ModelAdmin.list_display` may be a path across relations, "home__name", which `lookup_field` walks (`django/contrib/admin/utils.py:lookup_field`).
Since 6.1 a path ending at a boolean field draws the boolean icon; since 5.0 a property draws it when its getter has `"boolean"` (`django/contrib/admin/templatetags/admin_list.py:items_for_result`).

Since 5.2 a model's URL field is a link in read-only fields and in the list, unless its column is the row's link to the change form (`django/contrib/admin/utils.py:display_for_field`); a later security release keeps a value `URLValidator` refuses as text ([Security fixes: disclosure, spoofing and privilege](security-fixes-exposure.md); [The change list's columns: `list_display` and `list_editable`](../admin/list-display.md)).
With `ModelAdmin.list_select_related` false, the default, a change list showing a foreign key used to fetch, in the release notes' words, all foreign key fields (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).

Since 6.1 `ChangeList.apply_select_related` joins only what `ChangeList.get_select_related_fields`, which replaced has_related_field_in_list_display, finds: each column that names a foreign key or one-to-one field by its own name (`django/contrib/admin/views/main.py:ChangeList.get_select_related_fields`).

`True` is deprecated in 6.1, to raise `ValueError` in Django 2028: `ModelAdmin.__init_subclass__` warns as a class that sets it is defined, and `ModelAdmin.get_changelist_instance` when `ModelAdmin.get_list_select_related` returns it though the attribute is not `True` (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.get_changelist_instance`).

At this commit `ModelAdmin.log_addition`, `ModelAdmin.log_change` and `log_deletions` all write through `log_actions`, which saves one entry with `Model.save` and several with one `QuerySet.bulk_create` (`django/contrib/admin/models.py:LogEntryManager.log_actions`).

An override of log_deletion, or a manager's log_action, is not called at this commit, and nothing warns: the admin calls only the plural names (`django/contrib/admin/actions.py:delete_selected`, `django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin._delete_view`).

`BaseModelAdmin.delete_confirmation_max_display` (6.1) limits the lists of objects on the delete page, on `delete_selected`'s and in an inline's refusal to delete protected rows, giving the rest as a count; `None`, the default, sets no limit (`django/contrib/admin/templatetags/admin_filters.py:truncated_unordered_list`, `django/contrib/admin/options.py:InlineModelAdmin.get_formset`; [Deleting: `delete_view` and `get_deleted_objects`](../admin/deleting.md)).

`AdminSite.get_model_admin` (5.0) returns a model's model admin or raises `NotRegistered`, which, with `AlreadyRegistered`, is defined in `django/contrib/admin/exceptions.py` since 5.0; `django.contrib.admin.sites` imports both, so the old import gives the same classes (`django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.get_model_admin`).

`AdminSite.get_model_admin` (5.0) returns a model's model admin or raises `NotRegistered`, which, with `AlreadyRegistered`, is defined in `django/contrib/admin/exceptions.py` since 5.0; `django.contrib.admin.sites` imports both, so the old import gives the same classes (`django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.get_model_admin`).
`AdminSite.password_change_form` (6.0) names the password change's form, the admin's own when it is `None` (`django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.password_change`).
Since 6.1 `AdminSite.login` sends a user already let in to the request's `"next"`, when it is safe, and no longer always to the index (`django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.login`).

In 6.2 two views began to ask the permission before they answer an object's absence, so a user without it gets 403 whether the object exists or not: `ModelAdmin.history_view`, which, the release notes say, checked the existence first, and `AdminSite.shortcut_view`, behind "View on site", which asks the registered model's `BaseModelAdmin.has_view_permission` (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.history_view`, `django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.shortcut_view`; [Permissions in the admin: `has_change_permission` and the others](../admin/admin-permissions.md)).

Since 6.1 the change form puts each field below its label, the help text and then the errors between the two; a checkbox keeps the old layout (`django/contrib/admin/templates/admin/includes/fieldset.html`).

The class wide, which the new layout made obsolete, is gone, and the change form's `{% block object-tools %}` stands outside its `{% block content %}` (`django/contrib/admin/templates/admin/change_form.html`).

Since 5.1 a named fieldset with the class `"collapse"` is drawn in an HTML details element, unless one of its fields has an error, and collapse.js is gone (`django/contrib/admin/helpers.py:Fieldset.is_collapsible`); since 5.2 `"admin/base.html"` has `{% block extrabody %}` before the end of the body; since 6.1 the two-box select, `FilteredSelectMultiple`, keeps named groups of choices ([The admin's widgets: related objects, raw ids and autocomplete](../admin/widgets.md)).

Of the undocumented pieces, django.contrib.admin.helpers.checkbox was removed in 5.0, and the module django.contrib.admin.tests in 6.2; `InclusionAdminNode.__init__` takes the tag's name first since 6.1 (`django/contrib/admin/templatetags/base.py:InclusionAdminNode.__init__`).
Since 5.2 admindocs shows a model only to a user who may view or change it, asking the user and no model admin (`django/contrib/admindocs/views.py:user_has_model_view_permission`).

A link in a docstring may also carry its own text, the target after it in angle brackets (`django/contrib/admindocs/utils.py:split_explicit_title`; [The documentation generator: `django.contrib.admindocs`](../admin/admindocs.md)).
